problems.problem: The coverage DRAFT says 'Covered: body fat' and '9 may bear on your focus'. The rule accepts a review that names Asian people OR people without diabetes, so 7 of the 9 are fatty-liver or type 2 diabetes reviews, or non-Asian reviews. No review covers body fat in Asian people without diabetes. The two reviews closest to the focus (#7 and #8: obesity without diabetes, no significant change in fat mass) are not singled out.
problems.cause: Prompt Step 3 says to use 'the focus's own terms and the topic's population terms' but does not say how to handle a population with several parts. The kit has no Step 3 classifier, so the agent wrote its own OR rule in env/stir_l4_local.py.
problems.fix: Add to prompt Step 3: 'When the population has several parts, a review may bear on the focus only if it names the focus in its own sense and every part. List reviews that name only some parts in the broader table, naming the missing part. In the coverage DRAFT write "covered for <population named>", never a bare "covered".' Add kit k.select_reviews(population_parts=[...], require="all")

problems.problem: Question 1 joined 'Is everything above right? Reply "yes"' with the population a/b choice. The terse 'yes' (msg 13) settled only the first part, so the population was asked again at msg 18. That cost an extra turn, delayed the Team's Purpose line and the first FACT, annoyed the persona (self-reports after msgs 18 and 20) and caused the miss on M7(b).
problems.cause: Prompt 2b asks one reply to cover the reflection confirmation, the purpose numbers, the 'learning means' either-or and the population check, under a cap of three numbered questions, so two of them get merged.
problems.fix: Prompt 2b: 'Make the population either-or its own numbered question that "yes" cannot answer ("1. Keep the focus a) within <population>, or b) with no population limit?"). Fold the reflection confirmation into the purpose question ("2. If the summary is right, give the numbers of the kinds of purpose; otherwise say what to change"). When three items are already asked, apply the "both included" default for an ambiguous motivation instead of asking.'

problems.problem: The topic search found exactly 1 PubMed review (PMID 36212248, 2022, SGLT2 inhibitors for weight loss in obesity without diabetes), but the reply never names it; it is hidden behind 'show broader'. The code put it in the 'same drug and population' group only because 'Indonesia' matched the language phrase 'written in Bahasa Indonesia'.
problems.cause: The kit has no Step 3 selection function, and the agent's population regex matches country and language names anywhere in the abstract. The prompt lets the broader table wait behind 'show'.
problems.fix: Kit: ship k.select_reviews with population matching that ignores language and database contexts ('written in ...', 'Bahasa', 'China National Knowledge Infrastructure', 'Chinese Biomedical Literature Database') and flags population hits for a member to confirm. Prompt Step 3: 'When the topic search returns five or fewer records, name each one (title, year) in a FACT line, whatever group it falls in.'

problems.problem: The reply runs about 2,000 words: 294 prose words (prompt limit 180), four full cards with block tables, a 9-row review table plus a separate 9-row end-date table, a coverage table, a not-searched table and an 18-entry Sources line. The persona could not see 'the search strategy' at a glance and asked for it (msg 23).
problems.cause: The kit's k.review_table has no search-end column, so the agent added a second table. Prompt Step 3 requires two full cards per source in the first search reply and gives no compact overview first. The 180-word check was not enforced.
problems.fix: Kit: add an end_date column to k.review_table so there is one table. Prompt, 'How to talk' item 3: 'In a reply that runs more than two searches, put the compact strategy table (k.search_report(compact=True), one row per search) right after the FACT lines, then the full cards. Keep prose within 180 words by putting the field-tag key inside the first card.'

problems.problem: The FACT line 'PubMed's review filter finds no published protocols for your topic or focus' overstates what was counted: 0 records with 'protocol' in the title within the systematic-review filter. Protocols titled otherwise, or not yet indexed, are not ruled out.
problems.cause: The rule against overstating a count (R7) is general; the kit's search_report gives no FACT-sentence template for a variant search, so the agent paraphrased.
problems.fix: Kit: have k.search_report write the FACT sentence from the card ('0 records with "protocol" in the title [2]'). Prompt R7: add 'Never write that something does not exist; write what the search counted.'

problems.problem: Three log records misstate what happened. L000036 says Uday 'Chose' three kinds of motivation, but he replied 'yes' without choosing; including both kinds was the agent's default. L000087 logged a count read by eye ('2'), withdrawn in L000089. L000090 is marked 'Shown to Uday' but was replaced before it was shown (L000092).
problems.cause: The kit's k.confirm_states always records the member as the actor, even when the agent applied a default. The agent logged drafts before the reply was final.
problems.fix: Kit: give confirm_states a basis argument (chosen or default); for a default, log actor 'agent' with the text 'Both kinds included by default; not chosen'. Prompt 3.5: 'Log a draft with k.draft only once it is in the reply you send; never type a literature count into a log record.'

problems.problem: The Done lines say 'This may change the Individual Motivation you approved ... nothing changes unless you agree', but narrowing the focus to a population does not change Uday's motivations (learn; curiosity; publish). The persona asked himself 'should I redo it or not?' (self-report after msg 20).
problems.cause: The agent used the 'may change' template instead of the 'still stands' clause in the flow-tracing rule (R4). The prompt's template does not tell the team what action, if any, it needs.
problems.fix: Prompt, 'How to talk' item 2: 'When the reached decision's wording would stay the same, write "<decision> still stands". Otherwise write "This may change <decision>, because <flow>; say \"back\" to reopen it, or nothing to keep it."'

problems.problem: The reason-question reply has no Next line and no example. The self-report after it says knows_what_is_next=false.
problems.cause: The prompt's Certifying paragraph restricts this reply to the status line, one Done line and Your turn.
problems.fix: Prompt, Certifying paragraph: change it to 'the reply holds the status line, one Done line, "Next: I will record your certification and show <next item>" and Your turn: "What is your reason, in a few words?"'

problems.problem: The optional email request appeared three times although the persona ignored it each time, and he called it noise (self-report for msg 27). Meanwhile, the persona card's expected model-name item never appeared.
problems.cause: Prompt item 6 shows When-convenient items at the set-up, on 'where are we' and in the pause summary, with no limit after an item is ignored. The model name is deferred to Step 11, which disagrees with persona moment 5.
problems.fix: Prompt item 6: 'Show an optional item at the set-up and at most once more, in the pause summary. Drop it after it has been ignored twice.' Then align the persona card or Step 2d on when the model name is asked.

problems.problem: Several 'Says' quotes run 17-25 words, above the prompt's 'about 15 words'. The reply says the other records 'are also beside the chat' without naming the file.
problems.cause: The kit's review_table cuts a 25-word window (10 words before the hit, 15 after). check_reply only checks that 'show all' is offered, not that the opened file is named.
problems.fix: Kit: change the review_table window to 5 words before and 10 after (about 15 words). Make k.check_reply flag 'beside the chat' when the reply does not name the opened file, and add to the prompt: 'name the file you open beside the chat, in plain words.'

judge.strengths: I checked the files directly, and fidelity is clean. All 19 searches match the counts in the saved raw responses, and the quotes, years, PMIDs and search end dates match the saved abstracts. Certification was handled exactly: a bare 'Certify' got one reason question, 'just start' was never taken as approval, and the certified wording is identical to what was shown. Commits use the neutral 'STIR-L4 assistant' identity, and no email or key is in any file. The focus was drawn out with the two prompt probes, never supplied, and 'Added by me: nothing' is true. The focus is quoted in the status line, the Team's Purpose and the Step 3 search labels. Search display is complete: every block has its exact string, origin, count and date bound, a Sources line and a 'Left out on purpose' line, and the PubMed warning about the phrase 'absence of diabetes' was surfaced. The early move to Step 3 was announced and flagged in the status line. 'what was the search strategy?' got the compact table with no file pointer, and 'what's the next step?' got the plan map. The pause summary and map were shown in the chat, with the package made only at the pause. Plain language held throughout: no element codes, rule numbers or log ids in sentences, and terms explained at first use.
